From 3e3138007887504ee9206d0bfb5acb062c600025 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Keenan Dong <keenanat2000@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 13:12:40 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] rxrpc: fix RESPONSE authenticator parser OOB read

rxgk_verify_authenticator() copies auth_len bytes into a temporary
buffer and then passes p + auth_len as the parser limit to
rxgk_do_verify_authenticator(). Since p is a __be32 *, that inflates the
parser end pointer by a factor of four and lets malformed RESPONSE
authenticators read past the kmalloc() buffer.

Decoded from the original latest-net reproduction logs with
scripts/decode_stacktrace.sh:

BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in rxgk_verify_response()
Call Trace:

 rxgk_verify_response()
   [net/rxrpc/rxgk.c:1103 net/rxrpc/rxgk.c:1167
    net/rxrpc/rxgk.c:1274]
 rxrpc_process_connection()
   [net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:266 net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:364
    net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:386]
 process_one_work() [kernel/workqueue.c:3281]
 worker_thread()
   [kernel/workqueue.c:3353 kernel/workqueue.c:3440]
 kthread() [kernel/kthread.c:436]
 ret_from_fork() [arch/x86/kernel/process.c:164]

Allocated by task 54:
 rxgk_verify_response()
   [include/linux/slab.h:954 net/rxrpc/rxgk.c:1155
    net/rxrpc/rxgk.c:1274]
 rxrpc_process_connection()
   [net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:266 net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:364
    net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:386]

Convert the byte count to __be32 units before constructing the parser
limit.

Fixes: 9d1d2b59341f ("rxrpc: rxgk: Implement the yfs-rxgk security class (GSSAPI)")
Signed-off-by: Keenan Dong <keenanat2000@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
cc: Marc Dionne <marc.dionne@auristor.com>
cc: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
cc: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
cc: linux-afs@lists.infradead.org

Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260408121252.2249051-13-dhowells@redhat.com

diff --git a/net/rxrpc/rxgk.c b/net/rxrpc/rxgk.c
index f9f5a2dc62ed..01dbdf0b5cf2 100644
--- a/net/rxrpc/rxgk.c
+++ b/net/rxrpc/rxgk.c
@@ -1164,7 +1164,8 @@ static int rxgk_verify_authenticator(struct rxrpc_connection *conn,
 	}
 
 	p = auth;
-	ret = rxgk_do_verify_authenticator(conn, krb5, skb, p, p + auth_len);
+	ret = rxgk_do_verify_authenticator(conn, krb5, skb, p,
+					   p + auth_len / sizeof(*p));
 error:
 	kfree(auth);
 	return ret;
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the `rxgk_verify_authenticator()` function within `net/rxrpc/rxgk.c`. The bug occurred when constructing the parser limit pointer: `auth_len` (a byte count) was incorrectly used directly as a pointer offset for a `__be32 *` variable, causing the end pointer to be inflated by a factor of 4. This allowed malformed RESPONSE authenticators to read beyond the allocated buffer. The fix converts `auth_len` from bytes to the number of `__be32` elements before adding it to the pointer.

**File:** `net/rxrpc/rxgk.c`  
**Change:** In the call to `rxgk_do_verify_authenticator()`, the fourth argument (the limit pointer) is modified from `p + auth_len` to `p + auth_len / sizeof(*p)`. This ensures the pointer arithmetic is performed in units of `__be32` (4 bytes each), matching the type of `p`.

**Relationship:** The single-file change resolves the KASAN slab-out-of-bounds error reported during `rxgk_verify_response()`. The fix is minimal and directly addresses the root cause—incorrect byte-to-element conversion—without altering any other logic.

Here is the root cause:
The bug is due to incorrect pointer arithmetic in `rxgk_verify_authenticator()`. The variable `auth_len` is a byte count, but it is used directly as an offset to a `__be32 *` pointer (`p`). Since `sizeof(*p)` is 4 bytes, the end limit pointer `p + auth_len` is inflated by a factor of 4, allowing an out-of-bounds read past the allocated buffer when parsing a malformed RESPONSE authenticator.

Here is the patch:
  */
 static int rxgk_verify_authenticator(struct rxrpc_connection *conn,
 				     const struct krb5_enctype *krb5,
 				     struct sk_buff *skb,
 				     unsigned int auth_offset, unsigned int auth_len)
 {
 	void *auth;
 	__be32 *p;
 	int ret;
 
 	auth = kmalloc(auth_len, GFP_NOFS);
 	if (!auth)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	ret = skb_copy_bits(skb, auth_offset, auth, auth_len);
 	if (ret < 0) {
 		ret = rxrpc_abort_conn(conn, skb, RXGK_NOTAUTH, -EPROTO,
 				       rxgk_abort_resp_short_auth);
 		goto error;
 	}
 
 	p = auth;
-	ret = rxgk_do_verify_authenticator(conn, krb5, skb, p, p + auth_len);
+	ret = rxgk_do_verify_authenticator(conn, krb5, skb, p,
+					   p + auth_len / sizeof(*p));
 error:
 	kfree(auth);
 	return ret;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>ret = rxgk_do_verify_authenticator(conn, krb5, skb, p, p + auth_len);</text>
Reason:
The pointer `p` is of type `__be32 *`, so `p + auth_len` advances the pointer by `auth_len * sizeof(__be32)` bytes instead of `auth_len` bytes. Since `auth_len` is a byte count, this inflates the end limit pointer by a factor of 4, causing an out-of-bounds read when parsing a malformed RESPONSE authenticator.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>ret = rxgk_do_verify_authenticator(conn, krb5, skb, p,
					   p + auth_len / sizeof(*p));</text>
Reason:
Dividing `auth_len` by `sizeof(*p)` (which is 4) converts the byte count into the number of `__be32` elements, so the pointer arithmetic yields the correct end limit for the allocated buffer. This prevents the out-of-bounds read.
